chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to His servants, and He is more knowing of what is hidden of things, and He has counted the number of every thing, and is more seeing of the seers, and more hearing of the voices, and closer than the jugular vein, nothing is hidden from Him, and nothing escapes Him, and no deed is lost with Him, and neither a good deed nor a bad one escapes Him. Indeed, Allah is Subtle, Acquainted, and He is over all things Powerful.
ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes of Allah regarding justice and knowledge of deeds in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to reinforce the Shia doctrine of divine justice (*Adl*), countering the Mu'tazilite and Ash'ari debates by affirming that Allah’s omniscience ensures no action escapes His knowledge. This serves as a theological foundation for the concept of *Hisab* (accountability), emphasizing that every deed, regardless of its magnitude, is preserved in the Preserved Tablet (*Al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*) for ultimate recompense.
